Instructions from: AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md

Pure-Bun Codex gateway: ChatCompletions <-> Responses for the Codex desktop/CLI
app, zero npm dependencies. Declared models route to chat (OpenAI-compatible)
*or* Responses providers; undeclared models pass through to the signed-in
ChatGPT backend. Distributed as a compiled binary (`bun run build` ->
`codextras`); run it wherever you install it and state/, logs/,
codextras.json resolve next to it.

## Commands

    codextras start|stop|status       daemonize via pidfile
    codextras catalog                 declared-models catalog
    codextras catalog-merged          capture native catalog + write state/merged-models.json
    codextras dry-run [alias]         render future config.toml without writing
    codextras apply [alias]           backup + switch ~/.codex/config.toml to codextras
    codextras restore                 restore the pre-codextras config.toml
    bun run build                     compile the binary (src/cli.mjs)
    bun test                          unit tests (stop the gateway first: port conflict)
    ./smoke/verify-after-switch.sh    live checks (needs gateway running + real upstream key)

## Architecture

    src/server.mjs          Bun.serve: /v1/responses, /v1/responses/compact, /v1/models, WS refused with 426
    src/adapter.mjs         chat + Responses builders (thinking envelope, efforts, include, store, stream_options)
    src/convert/request.mjs Responses items -> chat messages (reasoning, tools, images, compaction) + flattenToolsForResponses
    src/convert/tools.mjs   custom/freeform tool bridge (exec etc.)
    src/convert/stream.mjs  chat SSE -> Responses SSE lifecycle (responses upstream is proxied verbatim)
    src/convert/json.mjs    non-streaming chat -> Responses
    src/catalog.mjs         catalog entry generation + native merge + visibility overrides (supports_reasoning_summaries toggleable)
    src/codex-config.mjs    config.toml managed-block rendering
    src/compaction.mjs      compaction v1/v2 with kcr1: summary envelope (chat or responses per provider)

## Onboarding: configure a model

Edit `codextras.json`. Providers are OpenAI-compatible chat **or Responses**
endpoints; `provider.type` (or `wireApi`/`api`) selects the wire format.
`type: "openai-chat"` (default) → `/chat/completions` with Chat↔Responses
bridging (needed for DeepSeek); `type: "openai-responses"` →
`/responses` with verbatim Responses passthrough (needed for Muse Spark,
preserves `reasoning.encrypted_content` + true multimodal). All three
dimensions are toggleable per-model: vision via `inputModalities` +
`imagePassthrough`, wire format via `provider.type` *or* `model.wireApi`/`model.api`,
and reasoning via `reasoningInjection`/`disableThoughtHack` +
`reasoningSummary`/`supportsReasoningSummaries`. Quirks carry per-provider
differences as data (thinking envelope, effort aliases, stream_options,
`include`). Relative `apiKeyFile` paths resolve against the repo root.

Example (opencode-go provider + DeepSeek V4 Flash):

```json
{
  "gateway": { "port": 4200, "pathPrefix": "/_codextras" },
  "providers": [
    {
      "id": "opencode-go",
      "type": "openai-chat",
      "baseUrl": "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1",
      "apiKeyEnv": ["OPENCODE_API_KEY", "OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY"],
      "apiKeyFile": "./state/opencode-go-api-key.secret",
      "quirks": {
        "thinking": { "type": "enabled" },
        "efforts": { "low": "low", "high": "high", "max": "max" },
        "streamOptions": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "models": [
    {
      "alias": "deepseek-flash",
      "displayName": "V4 Flash",
      "provider": "opencode-go",
      "upstreamModel": "deepseek-v4-flash",
      "contextWindow": 1048576,
      "autoCompact": 900000,
      "efforts": ["low", "high", "max"],
      "defaultEffort": "high",
      "inputModalities": ["text", "image"],
      "imagePassthrough": false
    }
  ]
}
```

Then `codextras apply <alias>` and restart the Codex app (it caches the
catalog). `catalogOverrides` can force native-model visibility (e.g.
`{"gpt-5.2": {"visibility": "hide"}}`).

Dual-provider example (DeepSeek on chat + Muse Spark on Responses, same key):

```json
{
  "providers": [
    { "id": "opencode-go-chat", "type": "openai-chat", "baseUrl": "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1", "apiKeyEnv": ["OPENCODE_API_KEY"], "quirks": { "thinking": { "type": "enabled" }, "efforts": { "low": "low", "high": "high", "max": "max" } } },
    { "id": "opencode-go-responses", "type": "openai-responses", "baseUrl": "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1", "apiKeyEnv": ["OPENCODE_API_KEY"], "quirks": { "efforts": { "minimal": "minimal", "low": "low", "medium": "medium", "high": "high", "xhigh": "xhigh" }, "include": ["reasoning.encrypted_content"], "reasoningSummary": "auto", "store": false } }
  ],
  "models": [
    { "alias": "deepseek-flash", "provider": "opencode-go-chat", "upstreamModel": "deepseek-v4-flash", "efforts": ["low","high","max"], "defaultEffort": "high", "inputModalities": ["text","image"], "imagePassthrough": false },
    { "alias": "muse-spark", "provider": "opencode-go-responses", "upstreamModel": "muse-spark-1.2", "efforts": ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh"], "defaultEffort": "high", "inputModalities": ["text","image"], "imagePassthrough": true, "supportsReasoningSummaries": true, "reasoningSummary": "auto" }
  ]
}
```
Alternative single-provider toggle: set `"api": "responses"` (or `wireApi`/`targetApi`) per `models[]` entry to override the provider’s wire format — same `type` field works per-model. Vision (`imagePassthrough`), wire format, and `<thought>` hack are all toggleable.

## Hard-won constraints

- The managed block in config.toml must stay at the TOP of the file: root keys
  (`openai_base_url`, `model_catalog_json`) land inside whatever table precedes
  them otherwise, and Codex silently ignores them.
- Reasoning is preserved twice for **chat** providers: `reasoning_content` on
  assistant messages (the DeepSeek API contract when tools are present) AND a
  visible `<thought>` block (the model's only real memory). Never use
  `<think>`: the upstream's reasoning parser strips that exact tag from
  assistant content. **Responses** providers (Muse Spark) do not use this
  hack — they replay `reasoning.encrypted_content` via `include` + `store:false`
  and should disable it with `reasoningInjection:"none"` / `disableThoughtHack`.
  Muse’s `summary` is empty today (encrypted only).
- Custom tools (exec) are advertised as functions with a single required
  `content` string property and returned as `custom_tool_call` items (see
  convert/tools.mjs). This mirrors the proven LiteLLM bridge; the app's tool
  router rejects plain `function_call` items for freeform tools.
- Catalog entries require `experimental_supported_tools` and should set
  `prefer_websockets: false`; Codex falls back to its built-in catalog if the
  file fails to parse.
- WebSocket upgrades get `426` on purpose: Codex falls back to HTTP streaming
  immediately. Do not add a WS endpoint.
- `state/` and `logs/` hold secrets (gateway token, provider API key, catalog
  JSONs). Never commit them.

## Verification loop

1. `codextras stop && bun test && codextras start`
2. `./smoke/verify-after-switch.sh` (health, config.toml root keys, catalog,
   real upstream turn, compaction, WS 426)
3. `codextras apply <alias>`, then the Codex app must be fully quit and
   reopened to reload the catalog.

## Conventions

Bun-only, no npm dependencies, no build step. Match the existing style (ESM,
plain functions, minimal abstraction). Add unit tests for conversion logic in
test/gateway.test.mjs; live behaviors belong in the smoke script.

tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. Send one or more questions, each with a stable id that will be echoed in the answer.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` steers a running child at its nearest step boundary or starts a turn for an idle or ready child, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

tools.description:
Search the web for any topic and get clean, ready-to-use content.

      Best for: Finding current information, news, facts, people, companies, or answering questions about any topic.

      Query tips:
      describe the ideal page, not keywords. "blog post comparing React and Vue performance" not "React vs Vue".

query.description: Natural language search query. Should be a semantically rich description of the ideal page, not just keywords. Optionally include category:<type> (company, people) to focus results — e.g. 'category:people John Doe software engineer'.

tools.name: present
tools.description: Declare existing files accessible through the Session filesystem as final deliverables. When a file you create or update is an output the user asked to receive, you must call present after writing it and before your final response, including files created through Bash or code execution. Mentioning its path in your reply does not replace this call. The files must already exist. The user opens the current source files; their contents are not copied or preserved.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a direct continuable child by its agent id. If you are a resident continuable child, you may also target your direct parent. If the target is still working, the message steers its nearest step; if it is idle, the message starts a turn. This call returns no answer from the agent — only confirmation that the message was delivered. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts a turn while it is idle. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts a turn while it is idle. tools.name: todo_write

Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

1: # AGENTS.md
2: 
3: Pure-Bun Codex gateway: ChatCompletions <-> Responses for the Codex desktop/CLI
4: app, zero npm dependencies. Declared models route to chat (OpenAI-compatible)
5: *or* Responses providers; undeclared models pass through to the signed-in
6: ChatGPT backend. Distributed as a compiled binary (`bun run build` ->
7: `codextras`); run it wherever you install it and state/, logs/,
8: codextras.json resolve next to it.
9: 
10: ## Commands
11: 
12:     codextras start|stop|status       daemonize via pidfile
13:     codextras catalog                 declared-models catalog
14:     codextras catalog-merged          capture native catalog + write state/merged-models.json
15:     codextras dry-run [alias]         render future config.toml without writing
16:     codextras apply [alias]           backup + switch ~/.codex/config.toml to codextras
17:     codextras restore                 restore the pre-codextras config.toml
18:     bun run build                     compile the binary (src/cli.mjs)
19:     bun test                          unit tests (stop the gateway first: port conflict)
20:     ./smoke/verify-after-switch.sh    live checks (needs gateway running + real upstream key)
21: 
22: ## Architecture
23: 
24:     src/server.mjs          Bun.serve: /v1/responses, /v1/responses/compact, /v1/models, WS refused with 426
25:     src/adapter.mjs         chat + Responses builders (thinking envelope, efforts, include, store, stream_options)
26:     src/convert/request.mjs Responses items -> chat messages (reasoning, tools, images, compaction) + flattenToolsForResponses
27:     src/convert/tools.mjs   custom/freeform tool bridge (exec etc.)
28:     src/convert/stream.mjs  chat SSE -> Responses SSE lifecycle (responses upstream is proxied verbatim)
29:     src/convert/json.mjs    non-streaming chat -> Responses
30:     src/catalog.mjs         catalog entry generation + native merge + visibility overrides (supports_reasoning_summaries toggleable)
31:     src/codex-config.mjs    config.toml managed-block rendering
32:     src/compaction.mjs      compaction v1/v2 with kcr1: summary envelope (chat or responses per provider)
33: 
34: ## Onboarding: configure a model
35: 
36: Edit `codextras.json`. Providers are OpenAI-compatible chat **or Responses**
37: endpoints; `provider.type` (or `wireApi`/`api`) selects the wire format.
38: `type: "openai-chat"` (default) → `/chat/completions` with Chat↔Responses
39: bridging (needed for DeepSeek); `type: "openai-responses"` →
40: `/responses` with verbatim Responses passthrough (needed for Muse Spark,
41: preserves `reasoning.encrypted_content` + true multimodal). All three
42: dimensions are toggleable per-model: vision via `inputModalities` +
43: `imagePassthrough`, wire format via `provider.type` *or* `model.wireApi`/`model.api`,
44: and reasoning via `reasoningInjection`/`disableThoughtHack` +
45: `reasoningSummary`/`supportsReasoningSummaries`. Quirks carry per-provider
46: differences as data (thinking envelope, effort aliases, stream_options,
47: `include`). Relative `apiKeyFile` paths resolve against the repo root.
48: 
49: Example (opencode-go provider + DeepSeek V4 Flash):
50: 
51: ```json
52: {
53:   "gateway": { "port": 4200, "pathPrefix": "/_codextras" },
54:   "providers": [
55:     {
56:       "id": "opencode-go",
57:       "type": "openai-chat",
58:       "baseUrl": "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1",
59:       "apiKeyEnv": ["OPENCODE_API_KEY", "OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY"],
60:       "apiKeyFile": "./state/opencode-go-api-key.secret",
61:       "quirks": {
62:         "thinking": { "type": "enabled" },
63:         "efforts": { "low": "low", "high": "high", "max": "max" },
64:         "streamOptions": true
65:       }
66:     }
67:   ],
68:   "models": [
69:     {
70:       "alias": "deepseek-flash",
71:       "displayName": "V4 Flash",
72:       "provider": "opencode-go",
73:       "upstreamModel": "deepseek-v4-flash",
74:       "contextWindow": 1048576,
75:       "autoCompact": 900000,
76:       "efforts": ["low", "high", "max"],
77:       "defaultEffort": "high",
78:       "inputModalities": ["text", "image"],
79:       "imagePassthrough": false
80:     }
81:   ]
82: }
83: ```
84: 
85: Then `codextras apply <alias>` and restart the Codex app (it caches the
86: catalog). `catalogOverrides` can force native-model visibility (e.g.
87: `{"gpt-5.2": {"visibility": "hide"}}`).
88: 
89: Dual-provider example (DeepSeek on chat + Muse Spark on Responses, same key):
90: 
91: ```json
92: {
93:   "providers": [
94:     { "id": "opencode-go-chat", "type": "openai-chat", "baseUrl": "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1", "apiKeyEnv": ["OPENCODE_API_KEY"], "quirks": { "thinking": { "type": "enabled" }, "efforts": { "low": "low", "high": "high", "max": "max" } } },
95:     { "id": "opencode-go-responses", "type": "openai-responses", "baseUrl": "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1", "apiKeyEnv": ["OPENCODE_API_KEY"], "quirks": { "efforts": { "minimal": "minimal", "low": "low", "medium": "medium", "high": "high", "xhigh": "xhigh" }, "include": ["reasoning.encrypted_content"], "reasoningSummary": "auto", "store": false } }
96:   ],
97:   "models": [
98:     { "alias": "deepseek-flash", "provider": "opencode-go-chat", "upstreamModel": "deepseek-v4-flash", "efforts": ["low","high","max"], "defaultEffort": "high", "inputModalities": ["text","image"], "imagePassthrough": false },
99:     { "alias": "muse-spark", "provider": "opencode-go-responses", "upstreamModel": "muse-spark-1.2", "efforts": ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh"], "defaultEffort": "high", "inputModalities": ["text","image"], "imagePassthrough": true, "supportsReasoningSummaries": true, "reasoningSummary": "auto" }
100:   ]
101: }
102: ```
103: Alternative single-provider toggle: set `"api": "responses"` (or `wireApi`/`targetApi`) per `models[]` entry to override the provider’s wire format — same `type` field works per-model. Vision (`imagePassthrough`), wire format, and `<thought>` hack are all toggleable.
104: 
105: ## Hard-won constraints
106: 
107: - The managed block in config.toml must stay at the TOP of the file: root keys
108:   (`openai_base_url`, `model_catalog_json`) land inside whatever table precedes
109:   them otherwise, and Codex silently ignores them.
110: - Reasoning is preserved twice for **chat** providers: `reasoning_content` on
111:   assistant messages (the DeepSeek API contract when tools are present) AND a
112:   visible `<thought>` block (the model's only real memory). Never use
113:   `<think>`: the upstream's reasoning parser strips that exact tag from
114:   assistant content. **Responses** providers (Muse Spark) do not use this
115:   hack — they replay `reasoning.encrypted_content` via `include` + `store:false`
116:   and should disable it with `reasoningInjection:"none"` / `disableThoughtHack`.
117:   Muse’s `summary` is empty today (encrypted only).
118: - Custom tools (exec) are advertised as functions with a single required
119:   `content` string property and returned as `custom_tool_call` items (see
120:   convert/tools.mjs). This mirrors the proven LiteLLM bridge; the app's tool
121:   router rejects plain `function_call` items for freeform tools.
122: - Catalog entries require `experimental_supported_tools` and should set
123:   `prefer_websockets: false`; Codex falls back to its built-in catalog if the
124:   file fails to parse.
125: - WebSocket upgrades get `426` on purpose: Codex falls back to HTTP streaming
126:   immediately. Do not add a WS endpoint.
127: - `state/` and `logs/` hold secrets (gateway token, provider API key, catalog
128:   JSONs). Never commit them.
129: 
130: ## Verification loop
131: 
132: 1. `codextras stop && bun test && codextras start`
133: 2. `./smoke/verify-after-switch.sh` (health, config.toml root keys, catalog,
134:    real upstream turn, compaction, WS 426)
135: 3. `codextras apply <alias>`, then the Codex app must be fully quit and
136:    reopened to reload the catalog.
137: 
138: ## Conventions
139: 
140: Bun-only, no npm dependencies, no build step. Match the existing style (ESM,
141: plain functions, minimal abstraction). Add unit tests for conversion logic in
142: test/gateway.test.mjs; live behaviors belong in the smoke script.

116: async function* sseEvents(body) {
117:   const reader = body.getReader();
118:   const decoder = new TextDecoder();
119:   let buffer = "";
120:   while (true) {
121:     const { done, value } = await reader.read();
122:     if (done) break;
123:     buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
124:     let index;
125:     while ((index = buffer.indexOf("\n\n")) >= 0) {
126:       const block = buffer.slice(0, index);
127:       buffer = buffer.slice(index + 2);
128:       const data = block
129:         .split("\n")
130:         .map((line) => line.replace(/\r$/, ))
131:         .filter((line) => line.startsWith("data:"))
132:         .map((line) => line.slice(5).trimStart())
133:         .join("\n");
134:       if (data && data !== "[DONE]") {
135:         try {
136:           yield JSON.parse(data);
137:         } catch {
138:           // Ignore malformed SSE blocks; the stream continues.
139:         }
140:       }
141:     }
142:   }
143:   const data = buffer
144:     .split("\n")
145:     .map((line) => line.replace(/\r$/, ))
146:     .filter((line) => line.startsWith("data:"))
147:     .map((line) => line.slice(5).trimStart())
148:     .join("\n");
149:   if (data && data !== "[DONE]") {
150:     try {
151:       yield JSON.parse(data);
152:     } catch {
153:       // Ignore malformed trailing block.
154:     }
155:   }
156: }

190: function normalizeArgsForCodex(value) {
191:   if (value === undefined || value === null) return "{}";
192:   if (typeof value === "string") {
193:     const trimmed = value.trim();
194:     if (!trimmed) return "{}";
195:     try {
196:       JSON.parse(trimmed);
197:       return trimmed;
198:     } catch {
199:       return "{}";
200:     }
201:   }
202:   if (typeof value === "object") {
203:     try {
204:       const s = JSON.stringify(value);
205:       if (s) {
206:         JSON.parse(s);
207:         return s;
208:       }
209:     } catch {}
210:     return "{}";
211:   }
212:   return "{}";

215: function mapResponsesItemForCodex(item, toolNames, customNames) {
216:   if (!item || typeof item !== "object") return item;
217:   const t = item.type;
218:   if (t !== "function_call" && t !== "custom_tool_call") return item;
219:   let name = item.name;
220:   let callId = item.call_id || item.id;
221:   let rawArgs = item.arguments;
222:   if (typeof rawArgs !== "string" && rawArgs !== undefined && rawArgs !== null && typeof rawArgs === "object") {
223:     try {
224:       rawArgs = JSON.stringify(rawArgs);
225:     } catch {
226:       rawArgs = "";
227:     }
228:   }
229:   let args = typeof rawArgs === "string" ? rawArgs : typeof item.input === "string" ? item.input : "";
230:   // If upstream returned flat name (collaboration__spawn_agent), map to namespaced for Codex
231:   const mapped = toolNames instanceof Map ? toolNames.get(name) : undefined;
232:   const fallback = !mapped ? mapToolName(name) : undefined;
233:   const target = mapped || fallback;
234:   if (target) {
235:     name = target.name;
236:     item = { ...item, name, namespace: target.namespace };
237:   }
238:   // Custom tools: Codex expects custom_tool_call with raw input, not function_call with JSON
239:   const isCustom = customNames instanceof Set && customNames.has(name);
240:   if (isCustom) {
241:     const raw = item.type === "custom_tool_call" ? item.input : unwrapCustomToolArguments(args);
242:     return {
243:       id: callId,
244:       type: "custom_tool_call",
245:       status: item.status || "completed",
246:       call_id: callId,
247:       name,
248:       input: raw,
249:     };
250:   }
251:   if (t === "custom_tool_call" && !isCustom) {
252:     // Upstream mistakenly returned custom for a non-custom tool — normalize to function_call
253:     let normalized;
254:     if (typeof item.input === "string") {
255:       const trimmed = item.input.trim();
256:       if (!trimmed) normalized = "{}";
257:       else {
258:         try {
259:           JSON.parse(trimmed);
260:           normalized = trimmed;
261:         } catch {
262:           normalized = JSON.stringify({ content: item.input });
263:           try {
264:             JSON.parse(normalized);
265:           } catch {
266:             normalized = "{}";
267:           }
268:         }
269:       }
270:     } else {
271:       normalized = normalizeArgsForCodex(args);
272:     }
273:     return {
274:       id: callId,
275:       type: "function_call",
276:       status: item.status || "completed",
277:       call_id: callId,
278:       name,
279:       arguments: normalized,
280:       ...(item.namespace ? { namespace: item.namespace } : target ? { namespace: target.namespace } : {}),
281:     };
282:   }
283:   // Ensure function_call has arguments string
284:   if (isCustom) return item;
285:   return {
286:     ...item,
287:     name,
288:     arguments: normalizeArgsForCodex(args),
289:     ...(target && !item.namespace ? { namespace: target.namespace } : {}),
290:   };
291: }

293: function transformResponsesJsonForCodex(json, { toolNames, customNames, requestedModel, requestBytes }) {
294:   if (!json || typeof json !== "object") return json;
295:   json.model = requestedModel;
296:   if (Array.isArray(json.output)) {
297:     json.output = json.output.map((item) => {
298:       if (!item || typeof item !== "object") return item;
299:       if (item.type === "function_call" || item.type === "custom_tool_call") {
300:         return mapResponsesItemForCodex(item, toolNames, customNames);
301:       }
302:       // Some providers nest tool calls inside message content? Not for Responses.
303:       return item;
304:     });
305:   }
306:   if (!json.usage) {
307:     // Lazy fallback — caller will finalize if needed; keep shape for finalizeUsage
308:     json.usage = null;
309:   }
310:   return json;
311: }

313: async function streamResponsesTurn(upstream, { model, requestBytes, toolNames, customNames }) {
314:   const encoder = new TextEncoder();
315:   const decoder = new TextDecoder();
316:   // We need to rewrite tool names on the fly while proxying raw SSE.
317:   // Responses SSE is `event: <type>\ndata: <json>\n\n` — we parse each block, map tool items, re-emit.
318:   const reader = upstream.body.getReader();
319:   let buffer = "";
320:   let sawCompleted = false;
321:   let streamError = null;
322:   const stream = new ReadableStream({
323:     async start(controller) {
324:       try {
325:         while (true) {
326:           const { done, value } = await reader.read();
327:           if (done) break;
328:           buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
329:           let idx;
330:           while ((idx = buffer.indexOf("\n\n")) >= 0) {
331:             const block = buffer.slice(0, idx);
332:             buffer = buffer.slice(idx + 2);
333:             if (!block.trim()) continue;
334:             const lines = block.split("\n");
335:             let event = "";
336:             let data = "";
337:             for (const line of lines) {
338:               if (line.startsWith("event:")) event = line.slice(6).trim();
339:               else if (line.startsWith("data:")) data = line.slice(5).trimStart();
340:             }
341:             if (!data || data === "[DONE]") {
342:               if (data === "[DONE]") controller.enqueue(encoder.encode("data: [DONE]\n\n"));
343:               continue;
344:             }
345:             let parsed;
346:             try {
347:               parsed = JSON.parse(data);
348:             } catch {
349:               controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(`event: ${event || "message"}\ndata: ${data}\n\n`));
350:               continue;
351:             }
352:             // Map tool call items in output_item events
353:             if (
354:               (event === "response.output_item.added" || event === "response.output_item.done") &&
355:               parsed.item &&
356:               (parsed.item.type === "function_call" || parsed.item.type === "custom_tool_call")
357:             ) {
358:               parsed.item = mapResponsesItemForCodex(parsed.item, toolNames, customNames);
359:               if (parsed.item.type === "function_call" && parsed.item.namespace) {
360:                 // Codex expects namespaced function_call to carry namespace alongside name
361:                 parsed.item.namespace = parsed.item.namespace;
362:               }
363:             }
364:             // Also handle response.completed's output array (some providers send it as event data)
365:             if (event === "response.completed" && parsed.response && Array.isArray(parsed.response.output)) {
366:               sawCompleted = true;
367:               parsed.response.output = parsed.response.output.map((it) => mapResponsesItemForCodex(it, toolNames, customNames));
368:               parsed.response.model = model;
369:             }
370:             if (event === "response.completed") sawCompleted = true;
371:             // Rewrite model in response.created/in_progress if present
372:             if ((event === "response.created" || event === "response.in_progress") && parsed.response) {
373:               parsed.response.model = model;
374:             }
375:             const outData = JSON.stringify(parsed);
376:             if (event) controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(`event: ${event}\ndata: ${outData}\n\n`));
377:             else controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(`data: ${outData}\n\n`));
378:           }
379:         }
380:         // Flush remainder
381:         if (buffer.trim()) {
382:           const lines = buffer.split("\n");
383:           let event = "";
384:           let data = "";
385:           for (const line of lines) {
386:             if (line.startsWith("event:")) event = line.slice(6).trim();
387:             else if (line.startsWith("data:")) data = line.slice(5).trimStart();
388:           }
389:           if (data && data !== "[DONE]") {
390:             try {
391:               let parsed = JSON.parse(data);
392:               if (parsed.item) parsed.item = mapResponsesItemForCodex(parsed.item, toolNames, customNames);
393:               if (parsed.response) sawCompleted = true;
394:               controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(`event: ${event}\ndata: ${JSON.stringify(parsed)}\n\n`));
395:             } catch {
396:               controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(buffer));
397:             }
398:           }
399:         }
400:       } catch (e) {
401:         streamError = e && e.message ? e.message : String(e);
402:         debugLog({ dir: "stream_error", wire: "responses", model, message: streamError });
403:       }
404:       if (streamError || !sawCompleted) {
405:         // Let client know the stream was truncated rather than pretending it completed cleanly
406:         const msg = streamError || "Upstream stream closed before response.completed";
407:         debugLog({ dir: "stream_aborted", wire: "responses", model, sawCompleted, message: msg });
408:         controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(`event: error\ndata: ${JSON.stringify({ error: { message: msg } })}\n\n`));
409:       }
410:       controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(sseDone()));
411:       controller.close();
412:     },
413:   });
414:   return new Response(stream, { headers: SSE_HEADERS });
415: }

417: export function createServer(config, secret) {
418:   const prefix = config.gateway.pathPrefix;
419: 
420:   return Bun.serve({
421:     port: config.gateway.port,
422:     websocket: {
423:       open() {},
424:       message() {},
425:       close() {},
426:       drain() {},
427:     },
428:     async fetch(request) {
429:       const url = new URL(request.url);
430:       const apiPath = apiPathFrom(url, prefix, secret);
431:       if (apiPath === "health") {
432:         return json({ ok: true, service: "codextras" });
433:       }
434:       if (apiPath === undefined) {
435:         return json({ error: { message: "not found" } }, 404);
436:       }
437:       if ((request.headers.get("upgrade") || "").toLowerCase() === "websocket") {
438:         // Codex probes a WebSocket transport first and retries on 405; a 426
439:         // refusal makes it fall back to HTTP streaming immediately.
440:         return new Response(null, { status: 426, headers: { Connection: "close" } });
441:       }
442:       const blocked = guard(request);
443:       if (blocked) {
444:         const message =
445:           blocked === 403
446:             ? "Browser-originated requests are not accepted by codextras."
447:             : "codextras requests require Content-Type: application/json.";
448:         return json({ error: { message } }, blocked);
449:       }
450:       if (request.method === "GET" && apiPath === "/v1/models") {
451:         const merged = mergeCatalog(config);
452:         return json({
453:           object: "list",
454:           data: merged.models.map((m) => ({
455:             id: m.slug || m.alias,
456:             object: "model",
457:             owned_by: "codextras",
458:             display_name: m.display_name || m.displayName || m.slug,
459:           })),
460:         });
461:       }
462:       if (request.method !== "POST") {
463:         return json({ error: { message: "method not allowed" } }, 405);
464:       }
465:       const rawBody = await request.arrayBuffer().catch(() => new ArrayBuffer(0));
466:       let payload;
467:       try {
468:         payload = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(rawBody));
469:       } catch {
470:         payload = undefined;
471:       }
472:       if (!payload || typeof payload !== "object" || Array.isArray(payload)) {
473:         return json({ error: { message: "Request body must be a JSON object." } }, 400);
474:       }
475:       const inputs = Array.isArray(payload.input) ? payload.input : [];
476:       const compactionV2 =
477:         inputs.length > 0 && inputs[inputs.length - 1]?.type === "compaction_trigger";
478:       if (apiPath === "/v1/responses/compact" || compactionV2) {
479:         return handleCompaction(request, payload, apiPath, rawBody);
480:       }
481:       if (apiPath === "/v1/responses") {
482:         return handleTurn(request, payload, apiPath, rawBody);
483:       }
484:       return json({ error: { message: "unknown route " + apiPath } }, 404);
485:     },
486:   });
487: }

1: import { newId } from "../util.mjs";
2: import { fallbackFrom, finalizeUsage } from "../usage.mjs";
3: import { toolCallItem } from "./tools.mjs";
4: import {
5:   COLLABORATION_NAMESPACE,
6:   COLLABORATION_TOOL_DELIMITER,
7:   COLLABORATION_TOOLS,
8: } from "./request.mjs";
9: 
10: function splitFlatCollaborationName(name) {
11:   if (typeof name !== "string") return undefined;
12:   const prefix = COLLABORATION_NAMESPACE + COLLABORATION_TOOL_DELIMITER;
13:   if (!name.startsWith(prefix)) return undefined;
14:   const toolName = name.slice(prefix.length);
15:   return toolName ? toolName : undefined;
16: }
17: 
18: export function mapToolName(name) {
19:   if (typeof name !== "string") return undefined;
20:   const flat = splitFlatCollaborationName(name);
21:   if (flat) return { name: flat, namespace: COLLABORATION_NAMESPACE };
22:   if (COLLABORATION_TOOLS.has(name)) {
23:     return { name, namespace: COLLABORATION_NAMESPACE };
24:   }
25:   return undefined;
26: }
27: 
28: export class ChatStreamConverter {
29:   constructor({ requestedModel, requestBytes, toolNames, customNames }) {
30:     this.requestedModel = requestedModel;
31:     this.requestBytes = requestBytes || 0;
32:     this.toolNames = toolNames instanceof Map ? toolNames : new Map();
33:     this.customNames = customNames instanceof Set ? customNames : new Set();
34:     this.seq = 0;
35:     this.responseId = newId("resp");
36:     this.createdAt = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
37:     this.reasoning = null;
38:     this.message = null;
39:     this.tools = new Map();
40:     this.toolIndexId = new Map();
41:     this.nextToolIndex = 1;
42:     this.reasoningOutput = [];
43:     this.messageOutput = [];
44:     this.toolOutput = [];
45:     this.usage = undefined;
46:     this.finished = false;
47:   }
48: 
49:   sse(type, data) {
50:     this.seq += 1;
51:     return (
52:       "event: " + type +
53:       "\ndata: " + JSON.stringify({ type, sequence_number: this.seq, ...data }) + "\n\n"
54:     );
55:   }
56: 
57:   initialEvents() {
58:     const snapshot = {
59:       id: this.responseId,
60:       object: "response",
61:       created_at: this.createdAt,
62:       status: "in_progress",
63:       model: this.requestedModel,
64:       output: [],
65:       usage: null,
66:       error: null,
67:     };
68:     let out = this.sse("response.created", { response: snapshot });
69:     out += this.sse("response.in_progress", { response: snapshot });
70:     return out;
71:   }
72: 
73:   handleChunk(chunk) {
74:     const choices = chunk && chunk.choices;
75:     if (!choices || !choices.length) {
76:       if (chunk && chunk.usage) this.usage = chunk.usage;
77:       return "";
78:     }
79:     const choice = choices[0];
80:     const delta = choice.delta || {};
81:     let out = "";
82:     const reasoningDelta = delta.reasoning_content;
83:     if (typeof reasoningDelta === "string" && reasoningDelta) {
84:       out += this.reasoningDelta(reasoningDelta);
85:     }
86:     const contentDelta = delta.content;
87:     if (typeof contentDelta === "string" && contentDelta) {
88:       out += this.flushReasoning();
89:       out += this.messageDelta(contentDelta);
90:     }
91:     if (Array.isArray(delta.tool_calls) && delta.tool_calls.length) {
92:       out += this.flushReasoning();
93:       out += this.toolDeltas(delta.tool_calls);
94:     }
95:     if (chunk && chunk.usage) this.usage = chunk.usage;
96:     return out;
97:   }
98: 
99:   reasoningDelta(delta) {
100:     if (!this.reasoning) {
101:       const id = newId("rs");
102:       this.reasoning = { id, text: "" };
103:       let out = this.sse("response.output_item.added", {
104:         output_index: 0,
105:         item: { id, type: "reasoning", status: "in_progress", summary: [] },
106:       });
107:       out += this.sse("response.reasoning_summary_text.delta", {
108:         item_id: id,
109:         output_index: 0,
110:         delta,
111:       });
112:       this.reasoning.text += delta;
113:       return out;
114:     }
115:     this.reasoning.text += delta;
116:     return this.sse("response.reasoning_summary_text.delta", {
117:       item_id: this.reasoning.id,
118:       output_index: 0,
119:       delta,
120:     });
121:   }
122: 
123:   flushReasoning() {
124:     if (!this.reasoning) return "";
125:     const r = this.reasoning;
126:     this.reasoning = null;
127:     let out = this.sse("response.reasoning_summary_text.done", {
128:       item_id: r.id,
129:       output_index: 0,
130:       summary_index: 0,
131:       text: r.text,
132:     });
133:     out += this.sse("response.reasoning_summary_part.done", {
134:       item_id: r.id,
135:       output_index: 0,
136:       summary_index: 0,
137:       part: { type: "summary_text", text: r.text },
138:     });
139:     out += this.sse("response.output_item.done", {
140:       output_index: 0,
141:       item: { id: r.id, type: "reasoning", summary: [{ type: "summary_text", text: r.text }] },
142:     });
143:     this.reasoningOutput.push({
144:       id: r.id,
145:       type: "reasoning",
146:       summary: [{ type: "summary_text", text: r.text }],
147:     });
148:     return out;
149:   }
150: 
151:   messageDelta(delta) {
152:     if (!this.message) {
153:       const id = newId("msg");
154:       this.message = { id, text: "" };
155:       let out = this.sse("response.output_item.added", {
156:         output_index: 0,
157:         item: { id, type: "message", role: "assistant", status: "in_progress", content: [] },
158:       });
159:       out += this.sse("response.content_part.added", {
160:         item_id: id,
161:         output_index: 0,
162:         content_index: 0,
163:         part: { type: "output_text", text: "", annotations: [] },
164:       });
165:       out += this.sse("response.output_text.delta", {
166:         item_id: id,
167:         output_index: 0,
168:         content_index: 0,
169:         delta,
170:       });
171:       this.message.text += delta;
172:       return out;
173:     }
174:     this.message.text += delta;
175:     return this.sse("response.output_text.delta", {
176:       item_id: this.message.id,
177:       output_index: 0,
178:       content_index: 0,
179:       delta,
180:     });
181:   }
182: 
183:   flushMessage() {
184:     if (!this.message) return "";
185:     const m = this.message;
186:     this.message = null;
187:     let out = this.sse("response.output_text.done", {
188:       item_id: m.id,
189:       output_index: 0,
190:       content_index: 0,
191:       text: m.text,
192:     });
193:     out += this.sse("response.content_part.done", {
194:       item_id: m.id,
195:       output_index: 0,
196:       content_index: 0,
197:       part: { type: "output_text", text: m.text, annotations: [] },
198:     });
199:     const item = {
200:       id: m.id,
201:       type: "message",
202:       status: "completed",
203:       role: "assistant",
204:       content: [{ type: "output_text", text: m.text, annotations: [] }],
205:     };
206:     out += this.sse("response.output_item.done", { output_index: 0, item });
207:     this.messageOutput.push(item);
208:     return out;
209:   }
210: 
211:   toolDeltas(toolCalls) {
212:     let out = "";
213:     for (const tc of toolCalls) {
214:       if (!tc || typeof tc !== "object") continue;
215:       let callId = tc.id;
216:       if (!callId && typeof tc.index === "number") {
217:         callId = this.toolIndexId.get(tc.index);
218:       }
219:       if (!callId) continue;
220:       if (typeof tc.index === "number") this.toolIndexId.set(tc.index, callId);
221:       const fn = tc.function || {};
222:       let entry = this.tools.get(callId);
223:       if (!entry) {
224:         entry = {
225:           id: callId,
226:           name: typeof fn.name === "string" ? fn.name : "",
227:           args: "",
228:           outputIndex: this.nextToolIndex,
229:           done: false,
230:         };
231:         this.nextToolIndex += 1;
232:         this.tools.set(callId, entry);
233:         out += this.sse("response.output_item.added", {
234:           output_index: entry.outputIndex,
235:           item: toolCallItem({
236:             callId,
237:             name: entry.name,
238:             args: "",
239:             status: "in_progress",
240:             customNames: this.customNames,
241:           }),
242:         });
243:       } else if (typeof fn.name === "string" && fn.name && !entry.name) {
244:         entry.name = fn.name;
245:       }
246:       const argsDelta = typeof fn.arguments === "string" ? fn.arguments : "";
247:       if (argsDelta) {
248:         entry.args += argsDelta;
249:         for (let i = 0; i < argsDelta.length; i += 10) {
250:           out += this.sse("response.function_call_arguments.delta", {
251:             item_id: callId,
252:             output_index: entry.outputIndex,
253:             delta: argsDelta.slice(i, i + 10),
254:           });
255:         }
256:       }
257:     }
258:     return out;
259:   }
260: 
261:   flushTools() {
262:     let out = "";
263:     for (const entry of this.tools.values()) {
264:       if (entry.done) continue;
265:       entry.done = true;
266:       out += this.sse("response.function_call_arguments.done", {
267:         item_id: entry.id,
268:         output_index: entry.outputIndex,
269:         arguments: entry.args,
270:       });
271:       const item = toolCallItem({
272:         callId: entry.id,
273:         name: entry.name,
274:         args: entry.args,
275:         status: "completed",
276:         customNames: this.customNames,
277:       });
278:       const mapped = this.toolNames.get(item.name) || mapToolName(item.name);
279:       if (mapped) {
280:         item.name = mapped.name;
281:         item.namespace = mapped.namespace;
282:       }
283:       out += this.sse("response.output_item.done", { output_index: entry.outputIndex, item });
284:       this.toolOutput.push(item);
285:     }
286:     return out;
287:   }
288: 
289:   totalOutputText() {
290:     let text = "";
291:     if (this.reasoning) text += this.reasoning.text;
292:     if (this.message) text += this.message.text;
293:     for (const entry of this.tools.values()) text += entry.args;
294:     return text;
295:   }
296: 
297:   finish() {
298:     if (this.finished) return "";
299:     this.finished = true;
300:     let out = this.flushReasoning();
301:     out += this.flushTools();
302:     out += this.flushMessage();

#!/bin/sh
set -eu
# Run after: bin/codextras apply deepseek-flash
# Verifies the live switch without starting a full Codex session.

PORT=$(sed -n 's/.*"port": *\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' /Users/will/.agents/codextras/codextras.json | head -1)
if [ -z "$PORT" ]; then PORT=4200; fi
SECRET=$(cat /Users/will/.agents/codextras/state/secret)
BASE="http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/_codextras/$SECRET/v1"
CONFIG="$HOME/.codex/config.toml"

echo "1. gateway health"
curl -s --max-time 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health" || exit 1

echo "2. config.toml points at codextras (root-level keys)"
python3 - "$CONFIG" "$PORT" <<'PY'
import sys, tomllib
cfg = tomllib.load(open(sys.argv[1], "rb"))
base = cfg.get("openai_base_url", "")
cat = cfg.get("model_catalog_json", "")
assert base.startswith("http://127.0.0.1:" + sys.argv[2] + "/_codextras/"), "missing/incorrect root openai_base_url: %r" % base
assert cat.endswith("merged-models.json"), "missing/incorrect root model_catalog_json: %r" % cat
PY
echo "ok"

echo "3. merged catalog contains deepseek-flash"
jq -e '.models[] | select(.slug == "deepseek-flash")' /Users/will/.agents/codextras/state/merged-models.json > /dev/null
echo "ok"

echo "4. tiny non-stream turn"
curl -s --max-time 60 "$BASE/responses" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "deepseek-flash",
  "input": [{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Reply with exactly: ok"}]}],
  "stream": false
}' | jq -e '.status == "completed" and ([.output[].type] | index("message"))'
